title: Qoro Quantum Opens Cloud GPU Simulation Tier to Accelerate Large-Scale Circuit Emulation - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Quantum software and middleware developer Qoro Quantum has launched its cloud-based GPU simulation tier for general availability, providing managed high-performance compute infrastructure designed to run tensor-network and noisy quantum circuit simulations without manual cluster administration. Integrated directly into Qoro’s Python framework, Divi (qoro-divi), the managed environment allows researchers to dispatch circuit workloads from local scripts to remote NVIDIA A10G and T4 GPU clusters.

Algorithm development often encounters a classical memory wall as qubit numbers and entanglement scale beyond statevector limits (where 64 qubits require approximately 295 exabytes of RAM at double precision). Transitioning to cluster-based tensor-network methods typically forces algorithm developers to configure Slurm schedulers, containers, and CUDA drivers manually. Qoro’s platform automates this infrastructure routing through Divi, abstracting hardware provisioning behind a single backend declaration while managing resource allocation dynamically based on the workload’s entanglement profile.

In technical validation benchmarks, the team simulated a 64-qubit non-integrable transverse and longitudinal Ising chain where non-local Jordan-Wigner terms rule out free-fermion classical shortcuts. While parallel CPU nodes handled low-entanglement circuits efficiently, GPU acceleration was required to sustain higher matrix product state (MPS) bond dimensions (χ = 512) to curb late-time energy drift. Free developer accounts receive 1,000 compute credits upon onboarding to evaluate hybrid workflows.

Benchmark data and code examples are detailed in Qoro’s Technical Blog here, with developer documentation available on the Divi Documentation Portal here.
